statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks judged on the account page (sign-up + password-reset forms) and both of its submit flows. Served by a static Python http.server fixture (HTTP/1.0, directory listing at /), so server-side behaviour (POST /signup and /reset, response headers) reflects this host, not necessarily a production deployment.

page.framework: none (static HTML + one shared stylesheet, zero scripts)
page.notes: Account entry page titled 'Your account', h1 'Sign in or create an account'. It has 36 DOM elements, 0 scripts, 0 inline handlers and one stylesheet (../base.css, 3 KB) shared with sibling fixture designs. It contains two forms: #signup-form (email, new-password, display name -> POST /signup) and #reset-form (one email field -> POST /reset). There is NO sign-in form (no current-password field, and /signin and /login are 404). The single nav link 'Account' (aria-current=page) points to / (a raw directory listing). Both form actions answer POST with 501. Sibling directories (booking/, catalogue/, contact-lead/, event-registration/) are separate designs, are not linked from this page, and are out of scope: booking/ was audited in run 2026-10-09T00-06-22-914Z.

findings.summary: A returning user cannot sign in. The h1 promises 'Sign in or create an account', but the page has only a sign-up form and a reset form. There is no current-password field, no sign-in link, and the conventional routes do not exist. Existing account holders are pushed towards creating a duplicate account.
findings.evidence: form-probe: signInFormPresent=false. The only password input is #password with autocomplete=new-password, inside the fieldset legend 'Create an account'. allLinks contains only '/'. GET /signin -> 404 and GET /login -> 404. The desktop screenshot shows the 'Sign in' heading above a 'Create an account' form.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a dedicated sign-in <form> (separate from sign-up) with <input type="email" id="signin-email" name="email" autocomplete="username webauthn" spellcheck="false" required>, <input type="password" id="current-password" name="password" autocomplete="current-password" required> and a <button>Sign in</button>. Put it first, because returning users are the majority. Move 'Forgot your password?' next to it as a link to the recovery step, and make 'Create an account' the secondary path (MWG autofill-sign-in-form).

findings.summary: Both flows dead-end. A valid submission of 'Create account' (POST /signup) or 'Send a reset link' (POST /reset) returns 501 'Unsupported method', so the user lands on the host's raw error page with no confirmation, no retry and their input lost.
findings.evidence: form-probe POSTed filled, valid bodies: /signup -> 501 'Unsupported method ('POST')' and /reset -> 501. A GET of either URL -> 404. The console logged 'Failed to load resource: 501' for both. Confidence is medium because the host is a static fixture server, but this is what a user of this deployment gets.
findings.suggestedFix: Back both actions with POST handlers using POST-redirect-GET. Sign-up should go to a 'check your email to verify' page. Reset should go to a neutral 'If an account exists for that address, we have emailed a link' page (no account enumeration). On failure, re-render the form with the input preserved (never the password) and an error summary at the top (role=alert) with a retry.

findings.summary: A credential form (email + password) is served and posted over plain HTTP with no Content-Security-Policy and no X-Content-Type-Options, while the footer tells users their account is 'protected by a session cookie'.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: https=false; content-security-policy and x-content-type-options missing. doc-probe: nextHopProtocol http/1.0. #signup-form posts the password to http://127.0.0.1:8765/signup. The footer copy reads 'Your account is protected by a session cookie.' Confidence is medium: loopback counts as a secure context (isSecureContext=true) and the fixture host may not reflect production, but nothing in the response sets a policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve and post only over HTTPS. Send Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script' (enforced, not report-only), and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Once a session exists, set it as __Host-session with Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/. The page has no scripts, so a strict policy costs nothing (MWG security).

findings.summary: The reset field's label is the question 'Forgot your password?', not what to type. Assistive tech announces 'Forgot your password?, edit text, required' for an email box, sighted users see no 'Email' cue, and the reset form has no heading or accessible name to set it apart from sign-up.
findings.evidence: a11ytree: the textbox #reset-email has computed name 'Forgot your password?'. Its form has no name, while the sign-up fieldset is the group 'Create an account'. form-probe: reset-form headingOrLegend=null and the label text is 'Forgot your password?'. axe passes it because a label exists; this is a clarity problem, not a missing-label rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the recovery form a heading ('Reset your password', h2) and name the form with aria-labelledby. Label the field <label for="reset-email">Email</label>, and add a hint ('We'll send a reset link to this address') linked with aria-describedby.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only. There is no passkey (WebAuthn) option for sign-up or sign-in, and no /.well-known/change-password endpoint for password managers. Recovery relies solely on emailed reset links.
findings.evidence: doc-probe: PublicKeyCredential is available in the browser, but the page ships 0 scripts, so there are no navigator.credentials calls. No input carries autocomplete 'webauthn'. form-probe: GET /.well-known/change-password -> 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys: after account creation, prompt to create one (MWG passkey-registration / passkey-conditional-create). On sign-in, add autocomplete="username webauthn" plus conditional mediation (passkey-authentication), feature-detecting PublicKeyCredential and keeping the password form as the fallback. Serve /.well-known/change-password as a redirect to the change-password page.

findings.summary: Error handling relies only on the browser's transient validation bubble. Invalid fields get no persistent visual state or inline message, nothing says the fields are required, and no error region is announced.
findings.evidence: form-probe: both forms fail checkValidity() when empty (4 required fields, each 'Please fill out this field.'). cssUserInvalid=false, liveRegions=0, and no field has aria-describedby. The features census shows :user-valid 0 and no :user-invalid rule. There is no password-rule hint, so a server-side rejection would be the first time users learn the rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the native required/type=email constraints. Add input:user-invalid { border-color: ...; } plus an adjacent message revealed with input:user-invalid + .error-msg. Link hints and errors with aria-describedby, and render server errors in a role=alert summary. :user-invalid is Baseline widely available (MWG validate-input-after-interaction).

findings.summary: The sign-up form misses several input-assistance points from the sign-up guide: no 'Show password' toggle, no stated password rules (no minlength or pattern), no autocomplete token on 'Display name', and no spellcheck="false" on the email identifiers.
findings.evidence: form-probe: #password has type=password, autocomplete=new-password (correct), minlength=-1, no pattern and no aria-describedby. showPasswordToggle=false. #displayName has autocomplete=null. #email and #reset-email use autocomplete=username, which is correct per MWG autofill-sign-up-form, but neither sets spellcheck=false. The guide asks for a Show password toggle and validated password strength with clear messages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add spellcheck="false" to both email inputs. Add autocomplete="nickname" to the display name (or drop the field until it is needed). State the password rule in a hint linked by aria-describedby and enforce it with minlength (e.g. 8+) rather than composition rules. Add a 'Show password' toggle button with aria-pressed that switches type between password and text.

findings.summary: The only nav item, 'Account', is marked aria-current="page" but points to '/', which is a raw server directory listing rather than this page. The current-page cue is wrong for assistive tech and sighted users, and there is no way to reach classes, bookings or a home page.
findings.evidence: form-probe navLinks: [{text:'Account', href:'http://127.0.0.1:8765/', current:'page'}] while location is /account-recovery/. GET / -> 200 'Directory listing for /'. The a11ytree exposes the link with the current-page state, and base.css renders it at font-weight 600. Confidence is medium because the host is a static fixture.
findings.suggestedFix: Point 'Account' at this page's URL (or set aria-current only on the link that resolves to the current URL). Add the real top-level destinations named in the lede (Classes, Bookings) and a home link that is not a directory listing.

findings.summary: No browser-enforced defences protect this credential page: no HSTS, no clickjacking protection (no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options), no Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy. A framed copy of the password form could be overlaid by an attacker.
findings.evidence: headers primitive: strict-transport-security, x-frame-options, referrer-policy and permissions-policy all missing, and there is no CSP to carry frame-ancestors. The page hosts a password field, so clickjacking risk matters more here than on a content page.
findings.suggestedFix: Once on HTTPS, send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, CSP frame-ancestors 'none' (or 'self'), Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() (MWG security, privacy).

findings.summary: No dark mode: the page ignores prefers-color-scheme and does not declare color-scheme, so the bright #f4f5f8/#fff surfaces and light form controls stay the same for users who ask for dark.
findings.evidence: The screenshot under prefers-color-scheme: dark is visually identical to the default capture. The features census (complete, 1 sheet) shows color-scheme 0, light-dark() 0 and no prefers-color-scheme condition; the only @media is (max-width: 44rem). form-probe: no <meta name=color-scheme>.
findings.suggestedFix: In base.css add :root { color-scheme: light dark; } and a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) override of the tokens (--ink, --muted, --line, --paper, --wash, --accent). Optionally express them with light-dark() behind that fallback. Add <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> to avoid a flash, then re-check accent/ink contrast in both schemes (MWG dark-mode).

findings.summary: In forced-colours mode the buttons lose their boundary. They are styled with a background colour and border: 0, so once the system palette replaces the background, 'Send a reset link' and 'Create account' render as bare bold text with no visible control edge.
findings.evidence: forced-colors.png (forced-colors: active + prefers-contrast: more): inputs and cards keep system-colour borders, but the 'Send a reset link' button shows no outline or fill. base.css sets 'button { background: var(--accent); border: 0px; }'.
findings.suggestedFix: Give buttons a transparent border instead of none: button { border: 2px solid transparent; }. Forced colours then paint it as ButtonText. Alternatively add @media (forced-colors: active) { button { border: 1px solid ButtonText; } }.

findings.summary: body sets font: 16px/1.5, a fixed pixel size that overrides the user's browser and OS default text size. People who raise their default font size get no larger body text or form fields (page zoom still works).
findings.evidence: dom css: 'body { font: 16px / 1.5 system-ui, ... }'. Headings use rem, but body copy, labels and the inputs/buttons (font: inherit) stay pinned at 16px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a relative size: body { font: 100%/1.5 system-ui, ... } (or 1rem) so text and inherited controls scale with the user's text-size preference (MWG respect-os-text-scale).

findings.summary: The only render-blocking resource (base.css) is served uncompressed with no Cache-Control or validators, over HTTP/1.0, so repeat visits re-download it.
findings.evidence: har-summary hygiene: base.css is listed in missingCacheHeaders and uncompressedTextOver2KB (3179 B, content-encoding none). renderBlockingCandidates: base.css (parser-inserted, VeryHigh), confirmed in the DOM as a <link rel=stylesheet> in <head>. doc-probe: nextHopProtocol http/1.0. The absolute cost is small (5.4 KB total).
findings.suggestedFix: Serve static assets with compression (br/gzip), a versioned filename and Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3. Optionally inline the 3 KB of critical CSS.

findings.summary: The <title> is the generic 'Your account', with no site name and no task, and there is no meta description, so search results, tabs and bookmarks cannot tell this page apart.
findings.evidence: form-probe: title 'Your account', metaDescription=null. discoverability: metaDescriptionPresentInRaw=null (absent). The h1 'Sign in or create an account' is more descriptive than the title.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a task- and site-specific title, e.g. <title>Sign in or create an account - <Site name></title>, and add <meta name="description" content="Sign in to manage your classes and bookings, or create a free account.">. Modern Web Guidance has no SEO guide; this is the Lighthouse SEO bar.

findings.summary: This multi-page flow (account -> sign-up confirmation / reset confirmation) swaps pages instantly. There is no cross-document view-transition opt-in.
findings.evidence: features census (complete): @view-transition 0 and view-transition-name 0. There are 0 scripts, so there is no same-document transition either.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } } to base.css. It is a pure progressive enhancement; browsers without support navigate normally (MWG cross-document-transitions).
